<system-reminder>
## Swarm Mode

You are now in "agent swarm" mode. The user may send tasks that require a large number of parallel subagents.

## Workflow

You do not need to use TodoList to record this workflow.

1. First, you may need to do a small amount of exploratory work before deciding how to divide the task across subagents. You may not need subagents during this exploratory phase.

2. After exploring, if you are convinced no subagent is needed to complete the task, tell the user why and wait for further instructions; otherwise, continue with the appropriate delegation.

3. Once you have enough context, do not handle the main work yourself. Use AgentSwarm with a `prompt_template` containing the `{{item}}` placeholder and an `items` array for the requested or appropriate number of subagents, partitioning the problem so each item gives one subagent a distinct part of the work. Pass `subagent_type` when the whole swarm should use a non-default subagent profile.

## Coordination

- Give each subagent a distinct scope of work.
- Avoid duplicating work across subagents.
- Avoid assigning conflicting changes or responsibilities to different subagents.
- Remember that subagents have your full capabilities. Do not overload their prompts with excessive detail; only describe the necessary background and each subagent's specific task.
- Unless the user explicitly specifies a lower limit, do not try to conserve the number of agents. AgentSwarm supports up to 128 subagents and queues launches automatically, so decompose work as finely as possible while keeping subagent responsibilities non-conflicting; combine tasks only when they are genuinely inseparable. If the subagents only need to read, inspect, or report back without making changes, their scopes may overlap slightly.
</system-reminder>

payload.prompt:
You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this - finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool - does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only - your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

1	# Doxygen
2	
3	Doxygen is the de facto standard tool for generating documentation from
4	annotated C++ sources, but it also supports other popular programming
5	languages such as C, Objective-C, C#, PHP, Java, Python, IDL
6	(Corba, Microsoft, and UNO/OpenOffice flavors), Fortran,
7	and to some extent D. Doxygen also supports the hardware description language VHDL.
8	
9	## What Doxygen Does
10	
11	Doxygen can help you in three ways:
12	
13	1. It can generate an online documentation browser (in HTML) and/or an
14	   offline reference manual (in LaTeX) from a set of documented source files.
15	   There is also support for generating output in RTF (MS-Word), PostScript,
16	   hyperlinked PDF, compressed HTML, DocBook and Unix man pages.
17	   The documentation is extracted directly from the sources, which makes
18	   it much easier to keep the documentation consistent with the source code.
19	
20	2. You can configure doxygen to extract the code structure from undocumented
21	   source files. This is very useful to quickly find your way in large
22	   source distributions. Doxygen can also visualize the relations between
23	   the various elements by means of include dependency graphs, inheritance
24	   diagrams, and collaboration diagrams, which are all generated automatically.
25	
26	3. You can also use doxygen for creating normal documentation (as I did for
27	   the doxygen user manual and doxygen website).
28	
29	## Usage
30	
31	Doxygen is a command line based utility. Here are the main ways to use it:
32	
33	### 1) Generate a template configuration file
34	
35	```bash
36	doxygen [-s] -g [configName]
37	```
38	
39	### 2) Update an existing configuration file
40	
41	```bash
42	doxygen [-s] -u [configName]
43	```
44	
45	### 3) Generate documentation using an existing configuration file
46	
47	```bash
48	doxygen [configName]
49	```
50	
51	### 4) Generate a template file that controls the layout of the generated documentation
52	
53	```bash
54	doxygen -l [layoutFileName]
55	```
56	
57	If layoutFileName is omitted, DoxygenLayout.xml will be used as the filename.
58	If - is used for layoutFileName, Doxygen writes to standard output.
59	
60	### 5) Generate a template style sheet file for RTF, HTML or LaTeX
61	
62	For RTF:
63	```bash
64	doxygen -w rtf styleSheetFile
65	```
66	
67	For HTML:
68	```bash
69	doxygen -w html headerFile footerFile styleSheetFile [configFile]
70	```
71	
72	For LaTeX:
73	```bash
74	doxygen -w latex headerFile footerFile styleSheetFile [configFile]
75	```
76	
77	### 6) Generate an RTF extensions file
78	
79	```bash
80	doxygen -e rtf extensionsFile
81	```
82	
83	If - is used for extensionsFile Doxygen will write to standard output.
84	
85	### 7) Compare the used configuration file with the template configuration file
86	
87	```bash
88	doxygen -x [configFile]
89	```
90	
91	Compare without replacing environment variables or CMake type replacement variables:
92	```bash
93	doxygen -x_noenv [configFile]
94	```
95	
96	### 8) Show a list of built-in emojis
97	
98	```bash
99	doxygen -f emoji outputFileName
100	```
101	
102	If - is used for outputFileName Doxygen will write to standard output.
103	
104	### Additional Options
105	
106	- If `-s` is specified, the comments of the configuration items in the config file will be omitted.
107	- If configName is omitted, 'Doxyfile' will be used by default.
108	- If - is used for configFile, Doxygen will write/read the configuration to/from standard output/input.
109	- If `-q` is used for a Doxygen documentation run, Doxygen will see this as if QUIET=YES has been set.
110	- `-v` prints version string
111	- `-V` prints extended version information
112	- `-h`, `-?` prints usage help information
113	- `doxygen -d` prints additional usage flags for debugging purposes
114	
115	## Download
116	
117	The latest binaries and source code can be downloaded from:
118	* https://www.doxygen.nl/
119	
120	## Documentation
121	
122	Full documentation and manual:
123	* https://www.doxygen.nl/manual/
124	
125	## Issues and Bug Reports
126	
127	Use the issue tracker to report bugs:
128	* https://github.com/doxygen/doxygen/issues
129	
130	## Mailing Lists
131	
132	There are three mailing lists:
133	
134	* doxygen-announce@lists.sourceforge.net - Announcement of new releases only
135	* doxygen-users@lists.sourceforge.net - for doxygen users
136	* doxygen-develop@lists.sourceforge.net - for doxygen developers
137	
138	To subscribe follow the link to:
139	* https://sourceforge.net/projects/doxygen/
140	
141	## Source Code

143	Doxygen is hosted at GitHub:
144	* https://github.com/doxygen/doxygen

You are one of four agents reverse-engineering the BEHAVIOR of a compiled binary for a clean-room reimplementation benchmark.

## Hard rules (violating these disqualifies the whole project)
- The binary is at /workspace/refdata/original.bin (also /workspace/executable). It is Doxygen 1.17.0, a documentation generator. You may ONLY run it with CLI arguments/stdin and read the bundled docs (/workspace/README.md). NEVER decompile, disassemble, run `strings`/`objdump`/`nm`/`gdb`/`strace`/`ltrace` on it, or read its bytes in any way. No internet access, no searching for the original source code, no installing doxygen.
- Work in scratch dirs under /tmp (e.g. /tmp/explore_<yourname>). Do NOT modify anything in /workspace except writing your single deliverable spec file (see task).

## Context
- Reference outputs already captured in /workspace/refdata/ (Doxyfile.full.txt = `-g -` output, Doxyfile.short.txt = `-s -g -`, DoxygenLayout.xml, emoji.txt, rtf_ext.txt, help.txt, d_list.txt, version_*.txt, w/ = `-w rtf/html/latex` outputs, docgen_empty/ = a full doc run on an empty project incl. run_stdout.txt/run_stderr.txt/filelist.txt).

## Method
Probe systematically. For every behavior record: exact bytes of output (use `od -c`/`cat -A` when whitespace matters), whether it goes to stdout or stderr (test with `>out 2>err`), and the exit code. Write findings as a precise spec a programmer can implement from without re-running the binary. Include exact message templates with placeholders like <argv0>, <file>, <line> where parameterized.

## Your task
{{item}}

Write the spec to the file named in your task, then reply with a compact summary of the most surprising/important findings (10-20 lines).
items: TASK ID: cli — Write /workspace/spec/cli.md covering the CLI DISPATCH layer only (not config semantics, not docgen run internals): every flag documented in -h and -d output and README (-v -V -h -? --help -d -s -q -g -u -l -w -e -f -x -x_noenv -m -b -c), plus probes for undocumented ones. For EACH: exact output/messages, stdout vs stderr, exit code, argument arity errors (too few/many args), what happens when target files exist or are unwritable (e.g. `-g` in a read-only dir, `-w rtf` onto existing file), `-` stdin/stdout variants for each command that supports them, multiple/conflicting flags together (e.g. `-g -u`, `-s` alone, flags after the config name, `--` handling), how argv[0] appears in usage (test via a symlink/copy with a different name — copying the binary to /tmp for this is allowed), full exact text of `-d` output (already in /workspace/refdata/d_list.txt, verify), behavior of no-args in a dir without Doxyfile (exit code? streams?), and what `-m`, `-b`, `-c` do. Also: does `-l` with no arg write DoxygenLayout.xml; messages printed by -l/-w/-e/-f on success (exact text incl blank lines and stream); error messages for `-w` with wrong subcommand, `-e` with wrong arg, `-f` with wrong arg.

TASK ID: config_parse — Write /workspace/spec/config_parse.md covering CONFIG FILE PARSING semantics (feed configs via `original.bin -x <file>` or doc runs with tiny Doxyfiles; use `-x` to see resulting values): comment syntax (# and ##), quoting rules (double quotes, single quotes?, escapes like \" and \\, \n?), list values (space-separated? quoting items with spaces), `TAG += value` appending (incl. += on a tag never set), duplicates (last wins? first wins? error?), case sensitivity of tag names and YES/NO values, accepted bool spellings (YES/NO/true/false/1/0?), integer parsing errors, empty value (`TAG =`), whitespace around =, line continuation with trailing backslash, @INCLUDE and @INCLUDE_PATH semantics and error messages when the include is missing, $(ENVVAR) expansion (undefined var behavior), DOXYFILE_ENCODING effect, warning text+stream for UNKNOWN tags (exact format incl file/line), OBSOLETE tags (try e.g. USE_WINDOWS_ENCODING, CLASS_DIAGRAMS, SYMBOL_CACHE_SIZE, XML_SCHEMA, XML_DTD, PERL_PATH, MSCGEN_PATH, TCL_SUBST, COLS_IN_ALPHA_INDEX, LATEX_SOURCE_CODE, RTF_SOURCE_CODE, DOCBOOK_PROGRAMLISTING, GENERATE_ECLIPSEHELP, SHOW_DIRECTORIES, HTML_ALIGN_MEMBERS, MAX_DOT_GRAPH_* old names) — exact obsolete-warning format and whether the value is ignored, and malformed-line errors. # Doxygen

Doxygen is the de facto standard tool for generating documentation from
annotated C++ sources, but it also supports other popular programming
languages such as C, Objective-C, C#, PHP, Java, Python, IDL
(Corba, Microsoft, and UNO/OpenOffice flavors), Fortran,
and to some extent D. Doxygen also supports the hardware description language VHDL.

## What Doxygen Does

Doxygen can help you in three ways:

1. It can generate an online documentation browser (in HTML) and/or an
   offline reference manual (in LaTeX) from a set of documented source files.
   There is also support for generating output in RTF (MS-Word), PostScript,
   hyperlinked PDF, compressed HTML, DocBook and Unix man pages.
   The documentation is extracted directly from the sources, which makes
   it much easier to keep the documentation consistent with the source code.

2. You can configure doxygen to extract the code structure from undocumented
   source files. This is very useful to quickly find your way in large
   source distributions. Doxygen can also visualize the relations between
   the various elements by means of include dependency graphs, inheritance
   diagrams, and collaboration diagrams, which are all generated automatically.

3. You can also use doxygen for creating normal documentation (as I did for
   the doxygen user manual and doxygen website).

## Usage

Doxygen is a command line based utility. Here are the main ways to use it:

### 1) Generate a template configuration file

```bash
doxygen [-s] -g [configName]
```

### 2) Update an existing configuration file

```bash
doxygen [-s] -u [configName]
```

### 3) Generate documentation using an existing configuration file

```bash
doxygen [configName]
```

### 4) Generate a template file that controls the layout of the generated documentation

```bash
doxygen -l [layoutFileName]
```

If layoutFileName is omitted, DoxygenLayout.xml will be used as the filename.
If - is used for layoutFileName, Doxygen writes to standard output.

### 5) Generate a template style sheet file for RTF, HTML or LaTeX

For RTF:
```bash
doxygen -w rtf styleSheetFile
```

For HTML:
```bash
doxygen -w html headerFile footerFile styleSheetFile [configFile]
```

For LaTeX:
```bash
doxygen -w latex headerFile footerFile styleSheetFile [configFile]
```

### 6) Generate an RTF extensions file

```bash
doxygen -e rtf extensionsFile
```

If - is used for extensionsFile Doxygen will write to standard output.

### 7) Compare the used configuration file with the template configuration file

```bash
doxygen -x [configFile]
```

Compare without replacing environment variables or CMake type replacement variables:
```bash
doxygen -x_noenv [configFile]
```

### 8) Show a list of built-in emojis

```bash
doxygen -f emoji outputFileName
```

# Doxygen

Doxygen is the de facto standard tool for generating documentation from
annotated C++ sources, but it also supports other popular programming
languages such as C, Objective-C, C#, PHP, Java, Python, IDL
(Corba, Microsoft, and UNO/OpenOffice flavors), Fortran,
and to some extent D. Doxygen also supports the hardware description language VHDL.

## What Doxygen Does

Doxygen can help you in three ways:

1. It can generate an online documentation browser (in HTML) and/or an
   offline reference manual (in LaTeX) from a set of documented source files.
   There is also support for generating output in RTF (MS-Word), PostScript,
   hyperlinked PDF, compressed HTML, DocBook and Unix man pages.
   The documentation is extracted directly from the sources, which makes
   it much easier to keep the documentation consistent with the source code.

2. You can configure doxygen to extract the code structure from undocumented
   source files. This is very useful to quickly find your way in large
   source distributions. Doxygen can also visualize the relations between
   the various elements by means of include dependency graphs, inheritance
   diagrams, and collaboration diagrams, which are all generated automatically.

3. You can also use doxygen for creating normal documentation (as I did for
   the doxygen user manual and doxygen website).

## Usage

Doxygen is a command line based utility. Here are the main ways to use it:

### 1) Generate a template configuration file

```bash
doxygen [-s] -g [configName]
```

### 2) Update an existing configuration file

```bash
doxygen [-s] -u [configName]
```

### 3) Generate documentation using an existing configuration file

```bash
doxygen [configName]
```

### 4) Generate a template file that controls the layout of the generated documentation

```bash
doxygen -l [layoutFileName]
```

If layoutFileName is omitted, DoxygenLayout.xml will be used as the filename.
If - is used for layoutFileName, Doxygen writes to standard output.

### 5) Generate a template style sheet file for RTF, HTML or LaTeX

For RTF:
```bash
doxygen -w rtf styleSheetFile
```

For HTML:
```bash
doxygen -w html headerFile footerFile styleSheetFile [configFile]
```

For LaTeX:
```bash
doxygen -w latex headerFile footerFile styleSheetFile [configFile]
```

### 6) Generate an RTF extensions file

```bash
doxygen -e rtf extensionsFile
```

If - is used for extensionsFile Doxygen will write to standard output.

### 7) Compare the used configuration file with the template configuration file

```bash
doxygen -x [configFile]
```

Compare without replacing environment variables or CMake type replacement variables:
```bash
doxygen -x_noenv [configFile]
```

### 8) Show a list of built-in emojis

```bash
doxygen -f emoji outputFileName
```

# Spec: Doxygen 1.17.0 configuration-file parsing semantics

Binary: `/workspace/refdata/original.bin` (Doxygen 1.17.0, hash `9135bd68ddc9ea65023d967c75048a7a86a5d495`).
All behaviors below verified by feeding tiny config files to `original.bin -x <file>` (which parses the file and prints the diff against built-in defaults) and by splitting stdout/stderr (`>out 2>err`).

Conventions used below: `<F>` = file name **as passed on the command line** for the main config, or **as written in the `@INCLUDE` line** for included files (relative names are NOT absolutized). `<N>` = line number (see §11). All `warning:`/`error:` text goes to **stderr**; `-x` diff output goes to **stdout**.

## 1. Statement syntax

- One statement per (logical) line: `TAG = value`, `TAG += value`, `TAG=`, `@INCLUDE = file`, `@INCLUDE_PATH = dir...`.
- Whitespace (spaces/tabs) around the tag, `=`, and value is ignored; leading whitespace before the tag is fine. `PROJECT_NAME=X` works.
- Tag names are **case-sensitive**. `PROJECT_NAME` works; `project_name` / `PrOjEcT_NaMe` do not (see §10 warnings).
- Empty value (`TAG =` or bare `TAG =` with only whitespace): silently accepted. String/list tags become empty; bool/int tags keep their **default** with no warning.
- Duplicate tag assignments: **last wins**, no warning, exit 0.
- Parsing always continues after bad lines; warnings never change the exit code (stays 0). A known tag after an unknown tag on a later line is still applied.

## 2. Comments

- `#` starts a comment running to end-of-line, anywhere **outside** double quotes: full-line (`# x`, `## x`, `   # x`) and trailing (`PROJECT_NAME = X # trailing`) both work.
- `#` inside double quotes is literal: `"a # b"` keeps the `#`.
- A commented `@INCLUDE` (`# @INCLUDE = f`) is ignored.

## 3. Quoting and escapes

- **Double quotes** group values containing spaces: `PROJECT_NAME = "Quoted Name"` → value `Quoted Name`. The `-x` output re-quotes such values.
- Inside double quotes, `\"` produces a literal `"` (the only escape that is processed). `\\` is **not** collapsed — two backslashes stay two backslashes. `\n`, `\t`, `\x` etc. stay literal backslash+letter, both inside and outside quotes. Outside quotes, backslash is never special (except line continuation, §7).
- **Single quotes are not special**: `'Single Quoted'` stores the value **with** the quote characters.
- Multiple quoted/unquoted segments are merged into one space-joined value, with a warning:
  `warning: Invalid value for '<TAG>' tag at line <N>, file <F>: Value '<raw>' is not properly quoted`
  `<raw>` is the raw value text exactly as written (e.g. `"one" "two"` → value `one two` + warning; `"a # b" c` → value `a # b c` + warning).
- Unclosed quote: the opening quote is stripped and the same "not properly quoted" warning is emitted (`"unclosed` → value `unclosed`).

## 4. List values

- Space-separated items: `FILE_PATTERNS = *.foo *.bar`. Items containing spaces must be double-quoted (`"*.foo baz"`).
- `=` **replaces** the whole list (wiping built-in defaults).
- `TAG += items` **appends**: works on a tag never set in the file (appends to the built-in default list, e.g. `FILE_PATTERNS += extra.z` appends to the ~55 default patterns), and on a tag just emptied (`FILE_PATTERNS =` then `+= only.z` → exactly `only.z`).
- `+=` on a **non-list** (string) tag: value unchanged, warning:
  `warning: operator += not supported for '<TAG> +='. Ignoring line at line <N>, file <F>`
  (note: tag name in the message includes the literal ` +=`, and the phrasing really is "Ignoring line at line <N>").
- `-x` renders multi-item lists one item per line: first line `FILE_PATTERNS          = *.foo \`, continuation lines aligned under the value column, each but the last ending in ` \`.

## 5. Boolean values

- Accepted (case-insensitive): `YES`, `NO`, `TRUE`, `FALSE`, `1`, `0`. Verified: `yes`, `No`, `True`, `TRUE`, `false`, `1`, `0` all parse; quoted `"YES"` also accepted.
- Rejected: `on`, `off`, `Y`, `2`, `-1`, arbitrary words. Warning (stderr, exit still 0):
  ```
  warning: argument '<VALUE>' for option <TAG> is not a valid boolean value
  Using the default: <DEF>!
  ```
  `<DEF>` is the tag's built-in default (`NO`/`YES`). The tag is reset to the **default**, not to any previously assigned value in the same file (`QUIET = YES` then `QUIET = maybe` → final `NO`).
- Empty value (`QUIET =`): silently keeps the default (verified for both default-NO and default-YES tags).

## 6. Integer values

- Decimal only; no hex (`0x10` rejected), no floats (`5.5` rejected), no trailing junk (`7xyz` rejected), range-checked per tag. Example with `DOT_GRAPH_MAX_NODES` (range 0..10000, default 50):
  ```
  warning: argument '<VALUE>' for option <TAG> is not a valid number in the range [<MIN>..<MAX>]!
  Using the default: <DEF>!
  ```
  Out-of-range (`10001`) and negative (when min is 0) give the same message. Tag resets to default.
- Empty value: silently keeps the default.

## 7. Enum (string-choice) values

- Invalid choice (e.g. `CLASS_GRAPH = BOGUS`):
  ```
  warning: argument '<VALUE>' for option <TAG> is not a valid enum value
  Using the default: <DEF>!
  ```

## 8. Line continuation

- A trailing backslash at end-of-line joins the next line. The backslash+newline is replaced by **one space**; leading whitespace of the continued line is preserved. Example: `PROJECT_NAME = one \` + `   two three` → value `one     two three` (1 space before `\` + 1 from the join + 3 leading = 5 spaces).
- Works for any tag (`QUIET = YES \` + `NO` → value `YES  NO` → invalid-bool warning quoting the joined value).
- File may end without a trailing newline; last line still parsed.

## 9. `@INCLUDE` / `@INCLUDE_PATH`

- Syntax requires `=`: `@INCLUDE = filename` (double quotes around the name optional). Nested includes work.
- **Without `=`** the line falls through to the tokenizer and produces a cascade of per-token warnings (see §10).
- Resolution order: as given (relative names resolve against the **current working directory**, NOT the including file's directory), then each directory in `@INCLUDE_PATH` (space-separated list, may be set before the include). Absolute paths work.
- Missing include is **fatal**: stderr, exit 1, no stdout output:
  ```
  error: @INCLUDE = <name-as-written>: not found!
  Exiting...
  ```
- Extra tokens after the filename are parsed as further statements → e.g. `@INCLUDE = inc.cfg extra` includes `inc.cfg` and warns `ignoring unknown tag 'extra'` for the same line.
- Warnings raised inside an included file report `<F>` as the string written in the `@INCLUDE` line (e.g. `file incbad.cfg`, relative), with physical line numbers within that file.

## 10. Unknown / malformed lines — exact warning formats

All on stderr, exit stays 0, multiple warnings possible per line, parsing continues:

- `UNKNOWN_TAG = value` (token followed by `=`/`+=`, tag not recognized):
  `warning: ignoring unsupported tag '<TAG>' at line <N>, file <F>`
  This also covers case-mismatched real tags (`project_name`) and **fully removed** tags such as `TAB_WIDTH` (no longer exists in 1.17 — see §12).
- Stray word token not followed by `=` (bare `PROJECT_NAME`, or `TAB too`, or `@INCLUDE` without `=`):
  `warning: ignoring unknown tag '<TOKEN>' at line <N>, file <F>` — one per token; tokens split on whitespace and punctuation (`does_not_exist.cfg` → `does_not_exist`, `cfg`; underscores are part of tokens).
- Stray punctuation character (`=`, `@`, `.` not in tag position):
  `warning: ignoring unknown character '<C>' at line <N>, file <F>` — one per character; raw byte is printed (a UTF-8 BOM at file start yields three such warnings with the raw bytes 0xEF 0xBB 0xBF; the BOM is NOT stripped).
- So `= novalue` yields both `ignoring unknown character '='` and `ignoring unknown tag 'novalue'`.

## 11. Line numbers

- `<N>` is the **physical** line number in the file where the offending token/statement starts (1-based). For a statement spanning continuation lines, the line of the `TAG` is reported (a tag on physical line 1 with a 3-line continued value reports line 1; a tag on physical line 4 reports 4).

## 12. Obsolete tags

Recognized-but-obsolete tags produce (stderr, exit 0, value **ignored**, parsing continues):
```
warning: Tag '<TAG>' at line <N> of file '<F>' has become obsolete.
         To avoid this warning please remove this line from your configuration file or upgrade it using "doxygen -u"
```
(second line = exactly 9 spaces + text; note `of file` here vs `, file` in other warnings, and the literal string `doxygen -u`, not argv[0]).

Verified obsolete in 1.17.0: `USE_WINDOWS_ENCODING`, `CLASS_DIAGRAMS`, `SYMBOL_CACHE_SIZE`, `XML_SCHEMA`, `XML_DTD`, `PERL_PATH`, `MSCGEN_PATH`, `TCL_SUBST`, `COLS_IN_ALPHA_INDEX`, `LATEX_SOURCE_CODE`, `RTF_SOURCE_CODE`, `DOCBOOK_PROGRAMLISTING`, `SHOW_DIRECTORIES`, `HTML_ALIGN_MEMBERS`, `MAX_DOT_GRAPH_WIDTH` (old name), `DETAILS_AT_TOP`, `QTHELP_FILE`.

Special case — `CLASS_DIAGRAMS = NO`: after parsing completes, if `CLASS_DIAGRAMS` was set to `NO` **and** `CLASS_GRAPH` is currently `YES`, then `CLASS_GRAPH` is forced to `TEXT` (regardless of statement order, and even if `CLASS_GRAPH = YES` was written explicitly) plus:
`warning: Changing CLASS_GRAPH option to TEXT because obsolete option CLASS_DIAGRAM was found and set to NO.`
(singular `CLASS_DIAGRAM` in the text). If `CLASS_GRAPH` is `NO`, no conversion and no extra warning. `CLASS_DIAGRAMS = YES` has no side effect.

Not obsolete / notable counter-examples:
- `GENERATE_ECLIPSEHELP` is still a valid tag (no warning, value applied).
- `TAB_WIDTH` no longer exists at all → `ignoring unsupported tag` (§10), not the obsolete warning.

## 13. `$(ENVVAR)` expansion

- `$(VAR)` is expanded inline from the process environment, anywhere in a value including inside double quotes and mid-token (`pre$(HOME)post` works).
- Undefined variable → expands to **empty string**, silently (no warning).
- CMake-style `$(VAR:-default)` is **not** expanded; left literal.
- `-x_noenv <file>` behaves like `-x` but prints values **without** environment-variable substitution (`$(HOME)` shown literally).

## 14. Encoding

- The config file itself is always read byte-wise as UTF-8 (no BOM stripping; a UTF-16 file, BOM included, is parsed as garbage producing `unknown character`/`unknown tag` warnings — `DOXYFILE_ENCODING` inside such a file cannot rescue it because it can't be read).
- `DOXYFILE_ENCODING` is validated after parsing. An unknown encoding name is fatal (stderr, exit 1):
  ```
  error: Error: unsupported character conversion: '<ENC>'->'UTF-8'
  Check the 'DOXYFILE_ENCODING' setting in the config file!
  Exiting...
  ```
- With a valid encoding name (e.g. `ISO-8859-1`), raw non-UTF-8 bytes in values pass through unchanged in `-x` output (byte 0xE9 stays 0xE9); no transcode/validation of value bytes was observed even with `DOXYFILE_ENCODING = UTF-8`.

## 15. File-level errors and misc

- Missing main config file (`original.bin -x nope.cfg`): usage text (52 lines, starting `Doxygen version 1.17.0 (...)`) to **stdout**, then `error: configuration file nope.cfg not found!` to **stderr**, exit 1.
- CRLF line endings: handled silently (`\r` stripped).
- `-` as the config file name reads the config from **stdin** (works with `-x -`).
- `-x` output header (stdout, first line, always): `# Difference with default Doxyfile 1.17.0 (9135bd68ddc9ea65023d967c75048a7a86a5d495)`. Tag column padded to width 23 (`PROJECT_NAME           = `). Values containing spaces are double-quoted; embedded `"` re-escaped as `\"`; backslashes are NOT escaped on output.
- Exit codes: 0 for any combination of warnings; 1 for missing config file, missing `@INCLUDE`, bad `DOXYFILE_ENCODING`.

(singular `CLASS_DIAGRAM` in the text). If `CLASS_GRAPH` is `NO`, no conversion and no extra warning. `CLASS_DIAGRAMS = YES` has no side effect.

Not obsolete / notable counter-examples:
- `GENERATE_ECLIPSEHELP` is still a valid tag (no warning, value applied).
- `TAB_WIDTH` no longer exists at all → `ignoring unsupported tag` (§10), not the obsolete warning.

## 13. `$(ENVVAR)` expansion

- `$(VAR)` is expanded inline from the process environment, anywhere in a value including inside double quotes and mid-token (`pre$(HOME)post` works).
- Undefined variable → expands to **empty string**, silently (no warning).
- CMake-style `$(VAR:-default)` is **not** expanded; left literal.
- `-x_noenv <file>` behaves like `-x` but prints values **without** environment-variable substitution (`$(HOME)` shown literally).

## 14. Encoding

- The config file itself is always read byte-wise as UTF-8 (no BOM stripping; a UTF-16 file, BOM included, is parsed as garbage producing `unknown character`/`unknown tag` warnings — `DOXYFILE_ENCODING` inside such a file cannot rescue it because it can't be read).
- `DOXYFILE_ENCODING` is validated after parsing. An unknown encoding name is fatal (stderr, exit 1):
  ```
  error: Error: unsupported character conversion: '<ENC>'->'UTF-8'
  Check the 'DOXYFILE_ENCODING' setting in the config file!
  Exiting...
  ```
- With a valid encoding name (e.g. `ISO-8859-1`), raw non-UTF-8 bytes in values pass through unchanged in `-x` output (byte 0xE9 stays 0xE9); no transcode/validation of value bytes was observed even with `DOXYFILE_ENCODING = UTF-8`.

## 15. File-level errors and misc

- Missing main config file (`original.bin -x nope.cfg`): usage text (52 lines, starting `Doxygen version 1.17.0 (...)`) to **stdout**, then `error: configuration file nope.cfg not found!` to **stderr**, exit 1.
- CRLF line endings: handled silently (`\r` stripped).
- `-` as the config file name reads the config from **stdin** (works with `-x -`).
- `-x` output header (stdout, first line, always): `# Difference with default Doxyfile 1.17.0 (9135bd68ddc9ea65023d967c75048a7a86a5d495)`. Tag column padded to width 23 (`PROJECT_NAME           = `). Values containing spaces are double-quoted; embedded `"` re-escaped as `\"`; backslashes are NOT escaped on output.
- Exit codes: 0 for any combination of warnings; 1 for missing config file, missing `@INCLUDE`, bad `DOXYFILE_ENCODING`.

payload.resultSummary:
Spec written to `/workspace/spec/config_parse.md`. Most surprising/important findings:

- **Two distinct unknown-tag warnings**: `UNKNOWN = x` → `ignoring unsupported tag`, but a bare word (no `=`) → `ignoring unknown tag`; stray punctuation → `ignoring unknown character '<c>'`. A line like `@INCLUDE f.cfg` (no `=`) produces a cascade of 5 per-token warnings.
- **`TAB_WIDTH` is gone entirely** (→ "unsupported tag"), while 17 other legacy tags (USE_WINDOWS_ENCODING, SYMBOL_CACHE_SIZE, XML_SCHEMA/DTD, PERL_PATH, …) get the two-line `has become obsolete` warning and are ignored. `GENERATE_ECLIPSEHELP` is still valid.
- **CLASS_DIAGRAMS=NO has a live side effect**: forces `CLASS_GRAPH=TEXT` post-parse (even if `CLASS_GRAPH=YES` was set explicitly, either order) with a warning that says singular `CLASS_DIAGRAM`. No effect if CLASS_GRAPH=NO.
- Bools accept `YES/NO/TRUE/FALSE/1/0` case-insensitively (even quoted); `on/off/Y/2` rejected with a 2-line warning that **resets to default, not the previous value**.
- Ints: strict decimal + per-tag range; error message embeds `[<min>..<max>]!` and `Using the default: <def>!`. Enums have an analogous `not a valid enum value` message.
- Quoting: only `\"` is a real escape; `\\` stays two chars, `\n`/`\t` literal. Single quotes are literal characters. `"one" "two"` merges to `one two` with a `not properly quoted` warning; unclosed quotes are silently closed + same warning.
- `+=` appends to built-in defaults for list tags; on string tags it warns `operator += not supported for '<TAG> +='. Ignoring line at line <N>…` (sic).
- `@INCLUDE` resolves relative to **CWD, not the including file**; missing include is fatal: `error: @INCLUDE = <name>: not found!` + `Exiting...`, exit 1. Warnings inside includes cite the filename exactly as written (relative).
- `$(VAR)` expands inline even inside quotes; undefined → empty silently; `$(VAR:-def}` left literal; `-x_noenv` shows unexpanded values.
- Line numbers in warnings are physical lines of the statement's start; continuation `\`+newline becomes exactly one space.
- UTF-8 BOM is **not** stripped (3 `unknown character` warnings with raw bytes); UTF-16 config files parse as garbage; bad `DOXYFILE_ENCODING` is fatal with a 3-line error. CRLF is fine; `-` reads config from stdin; missing main config prints usage to stdout + error to stderr, exit 1.

# Spec: documentation runs & remaining generators (doxygen 1.17.0) Binary probed: `/workspace/refdata/original.bin` (== `/workspace/executable`), invoked as `` below. All findings verified by direct execution. `` = argv[0] as invoked. Version string constant: `1.17.0 (9135bd68ddc9ea65023d967c75048a7a86a5d495)`. Reference captures live in `/workspace/refdata/docgen_empty/` (empty-project run) and `/workspace/refdata/w/` (`-w` template outputs). All generated bytes referenced there were reproduced byte-for-byte. --- ## 1. Empty-project documentation run Setup that produced `/workspace/refdata/docgen_empty/`: cwd = the run directory, config = `/workspace/refdata/Doxyfile.full.txt` (i.e. `-g` output) plus one appended line `PROJECT_NAME = EmptyProj` (after line 2997). Command: ` Doxyfile` (or bare ``, which defaults to `./Doxyfile`; both behave identically). ### Exit code - `0` on success — **including** when there are no input files and warnings are emitted. - Warnings do NOT affect the exit code unless `WARN_AS_ERROR = YES` (see §3). ### Byte-stability Two identical runs (and the pre-captured refdata run, made at a different wall-clock time) produce **byte-identical** `html/` and `latex/` trees. No timestamps, no randomness, no hostname, no absolute paths are embedded in any generated file. The ONLY run-dependent byte in stdout is the absolute directory path on the `Searching for files in directory ...` line. ### stdout (exactly these 106 lines, in this order, LF-terminated, nothing else) ``` Doxygen version used: 1.17.0 (9135bd68ddc9ea65023d967c75048a7a86a5d495) Searching for include files... Searching for example files... Searching for images... Searching for dot files... Searching for msc files... Searching for dia files... Searching for plantuml files... Determining the scope of groups... Computing module relations... Sorting lists... Determining which enums are documented Computing member relations... Building full member lists recursively... Adding members to member groups. Computing member references... Inheriting documentation... Generating disk names... Adding source references... Adding xrefitems... Adding requirements... Sorting member lists... Setting anonymous enum type... Computing dependencies between directories... Generating citations page... Counting members... Counting data structures... Resolving user defined references... Finding anchors and sections in the documentation... Transferring function references... Combining using relations... Adding members to index pages... Correcting members for VHDL... Computing tooltip texts... Generating style sheet... Generating search indices... Generating example documentation... Generating file sources... Generating file documentation... Generating page documentation... Generating group documentation... Generating class documentation... Generating concept documentation... Generating module documentation... Generating namespace documentation... Generating graph info page... Generating directory documentation... Generating index page... Generating page index... Generating topic index... Generating module index... Generating module member index... Generating namespace index... Generating namespace member index... Generating concept index... Generating annotated compound index... Generating alphabetical compound index... Generating hierarchical class index... Generating member index... Generating file index... Generating file member index... Generating example index... finalizing index lists... writing tag file... Running plantuml with JAVA... type lookup cache used 0/65536 hits=0 misses=0 symbol lookup cache used 0/65536 hits=0 misses=0 finished... ``` Notes on individual lines: - Line 1 is always first for a doc run: `Doxygen version used: `. - `Searching for files in directory ` — one line per existing INPUT directory, in INPUT order. `` is the absolute path. With default (empty) `INPUT`, the bare cwd absolute path is printed with NO trailing slash (e.g. `/tmp/work`). With explicit `INPUT = .` the printed path HAS a trailing slash (`/tmp/work/`). Nonexistent INPUT dirs produce no such line (warnings instead, see §3). - `Running plantuml with JAVA...` is printed unconditionally (even with zero plantuml files, even with no input at all; java presence irrelevant). Likewise the two `... lookup cache used 0/65536 hits=0 misses=0` lines (empty project ⇒ all zeros) and `finished...` as the last line. - This sequence is **completely insensitive** to `GENERATE_HTML=NO`, `GENERATE_LATEX=NO`, `SEARCHENGINE=NO`, `DISABLE_INDEX=YES`, `CREATE_SUBDIRS=YES` — diffing stdout of those runs against the baseline shows only the cwd-path line differs. First line: `# Generated by doxygen 1.17.0`. `-` works. ### `-w html [configFile]` - Writes three files == `/workspace/refdata/w/{header.html,footer.html,style.css}` (2764 / 781 / 55207 bytes with defaults). - header.html and footer.html are **static templates** with literal `$placeholder`s (`$projectname`, `$title`, `$relpath^`, `$doxygenversion`, ...) and ``/`` conditional markers. payload.resultSummary:
Spec written to `/workspace/spec/docgen.md` (~21 KB). Key findings:

- **Byte-stability**: empty-project runs are 100% reproducible — the html/latex trees match refdata byte-for-byte across runs and wall-clock time. The ONLY variable byte in stdout is the cwd path on the `Searching for files in directory <ABS_DIR>` line.
- **stdout is a fixed 106-line script**: astonishingly, `GENERATE_HTML=NO`, `GENERATE_LATEX=NO`, `SEARCHENGINE=NO`, `DISABLE_INDEX=YES`, `CREATE_SUBDIRS=YES` produce *zero* changes to the stdout sequence — all `Generating ...` lines print even when nothing is generated. `Running plantuml with JAVA...` is unconditional.
- **Warnings always go to stderr and never change the exit code** (stays 0) unless `WARN_AS_ERROR=YES`, which rewrites the `warning:` prefix to `error:`, appends ` (warning treated as error, aborting now)`, prints `Exiting...` on stdout, exits 1.
- `QUIET=YES`/`-q` blanks stdout entirely (even the OUTPUT_DIRECTORY Notice) but keeps stderr; `-q` works in any arg position.
- `OUTPUT_DIRECTORY` creates only ONE missing level (`Notice: Output directory 'out' does not exist. I have created it for you.` as stdout line 2); nested missing dirs are a fatal `error: tag OUTPUT_DIRECTORY: ...`, exit 1.
- Config substitutions isolated by pairwise diff: PROJECT_NAME hits exactly 3 files (with LaTeX `\+` space-escaping in refman.tex), PROJECT_NUMBER 2 files, PROJECT_BRIEF 2 files; PROJECT_LOGO is copied byte-identical to html/ and latex/ but **not referenced in refman.tex**.
- Undocumented-input warning format: `<abspath>:<line>: warning: Member <name> (<kind>) of file <base> is not documented.` — only fires when the enclosing file IS documented; a fully undocumented .py is silent under defaults.
- `-w html` header/footer are static `$placeholder` templates — the configFile arg does NOT change them (even PAPER_TYPE for latex); but **style.css IS rendered from config** (HTML_COLORSTYLE_HUE/SAT recompute every color; FULL_SIDEBAR appends rules). `-w html - - -` concatenates all three to stdout.
- `-l`/`-w`/`-e`/`-f` are silent on success, overwrite without asking, `-` = stdout; all 10 arg-error strings captured exactly (stderr, exit 1).
- `-c` quirks: needs a Doxyfile or fails like a doc run; `-c missing.txt` with Doxyfile present exits 0 **silently**; `-c -` reads stdin; missing-arg message goes to *stdout* with the developer-params list.

args.content:
# Spec: config_serialize — Doxygen 1.17.0 config template generation, `-u` update, `-x`/`-x_noenv` diff

Binary probed: `/workspace/refdata/original.bin` (Doxygen 1.17.0, commit `9135bd68ddc9ea65023d967c75048a7a86a5d495`).
All outputs verified byte-stable across runs (two `-g -` runs byte-identical; identical to `/workspace/refdata/Doxyfile.full.txt` / `Doxyfile.short.txt`).

Conventions: `<name>` = config file name as given on the command line (default `Doxyfile`). All streams/exit codes verified by redirection.

---

## 1. `-g` template generation

### 1.1 Messages and streams

- `doxygen [-s] -g <name>` (writes a file):
  - File `<name>` is written (existing file **overwritten silently**, no prompt, no backup).
  - stdout, exact bytes (note leading and trailing blank lines):
    ```
    \n\nConfiguration file '<name>' created.\n\nNow edit the configuration file and enter\n\n  doxygen\n\nto generate the documentation for your project\n\n
    ```
    i.e. lines: ``, ``, `Configuration file '<name>' created.`, ``, `Now edit the configuration file and enter`, ``, `  doxygen` (two leading spaces), ``, `to generate the documentation for your project`, ``.
  - stderr empty. Exit code 0.
- `doxygen [-s] -g -` (stdout): writes **only the template** to stdout — no "created" message, no extra blank lines. stderr empty, exit 0.
- The file written by `-g <name>` is byte-identical to the `-g -` stdout output.
- `-s` selects the short template; `-s -g <name>` prints the same "created" message form.

### 1.2 Full template structure (`-g`, 2997 lines)

Reference bytes: `/workspace/refdata/Doxyfile.full.txt`.

Header (lines 1–25), verbatim:

```
# Doxyfile 1.17.0
<blank>
# This file describes the settings to be used by the documentation system
# Doxygen (www.doxygen.org) for a project.
#
# All text after a double hash (##) is considered a comment and is placed in
# front of the TAG it is preceding.
#
# All text after a single hash (#) is considered a comment and will be ignored.
# The format is:
# TAG = value [value, ...]
# For lists, items can also be appended using:
# TAG += value [value, ...]
# Values that contain spaces should be placed between quotes (\" \").
#
# Note:
#
# Use Doxygen to compare the used configuration file with the template
# configuration file:
# doxygen -x [configFile]
# Use Doxygen to compare the used configuration file with the template
# configuration file without replacing the environment variables or CMake type
# replacement variables:
# doxygen -x_noenv [configFile]
<blank>
```

Then 18 sections. Each section is a 3-line banner; in the **full** template the banner is preceded and followed by one blank line:

```
#---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# <Section title>
#---------------------------------------------------------------------------
```

The banner rule line is exactly `#` + 75 dashes. Section titles, in order:

1. `Project related configuration options`
2. `Build related configuration options`
3. `Configuration options related to warning and progress messages`
4. `Configuration options related to the input files`
5. `Configuration options related to source browsing`
6. `Configuration options related to the alphabetical class index`
7. `Configuration options related to the HTML output`
8. `Configuration options related to the LaTeX output`
9. `Configuration options related to the RTF output`
10. `Configuration options related to the man page output`
11. `Configuration options related to the XML output`
12. `Configuration options related to the DOCBOOK output`
13. `Configuration options for the AutoGen Definitions output`
14. `Configuration options related to Sqlite3 output`
15. `Configuration options related to the Perl module output`
16. `Configuration options related to the preprocessor`
17. `Configuration options related to external references`
18. `Configuration options related to diagram generator tools`

Per-option block in the full template:

```
# <comment line 1>
# <comment line ...>
<blank>
TAG<padding>= <value>
<blank>
```

- 306 options total, all emitted **active** (there are NO commented-out `# TAG = default` template options in 1.17.0; the only `# TAG = ...` lines are examples inside comment prose, e.g. `# MATHJAX_EXTENSIONS = ams`).
- **Alignment**: the tag name is left-justified padded with spaces to width 23, then `=`. So `=` is always at byte column 24 (1-based). The two 23-char tags (`HIDE_COMPOUND_REFERENCE`, `GENERATE_DEPRECATEDLIST`) get zero padding: `HIDE_COMPOUND_REFERENCE= NO`. Format equivalent to `printf("%-23s= ...")` — no extra space if tag length ≥ 23 (none exist longer in 1.17.0).
- Empty values: line ends right after `=`, **no trailing space** (`PROJECT_NUMBER         =\n`). Verified: zero lines with trailing whitespace in the whole template.
- Value starts at column 26 (after `= `).
- Multi-line (list) values: first item on the tag line; each subsequent item on its own line, indented with 25 spaces (item starts at column 26, aligned under the first item); every line except the last ends with ` \` (space + backslash); last item has no backslash. Exactly 59 continuation lines in the full template. Example:

```
ABBREVIATE_BRIEF       = "The $name class" \
                         "The $name widget" \
                         ...
                         the
```

- Quoting of defaults: a value/item containing a space is wrapped in double quotes (`PROJECT_NAME           = "My Project"`, `"The $name class"`); items without spaces are unquoted (`English`, `*.c`).
- Comment block conventions (generated from option metadata):
  - `The default value is: <value>.` — 193 options, final line of the comment for string/int/bool options with a non-empty scalar default. The `<value>` here is shown **unquoted** even when the emitted default is quoted (e.g. comment says `The default value is: My Project.` while the tag line is `PROJECT_NAME           = "My Project"`).
  - `Minimum value: <n>, maximum value: <n>, default value: <n>.` — 21 int options with ranges.
  - `Possible values are: ...` — 15 enum-ish options (list may wrap over several comment lines).
  - `This tag requires that the tag <TAG> is set to <VAL>.` — 147 occurrences (dependency notes; `<VAL>` observed: `YES`).
  - One special: `# Note: This tag requires that UML_LOOK isn't set, i.e. the Doxygen internal` (wraps to next line; for `UML_LOOK`-adjacent option).
  - `See also: <TAG>` lines appear for some options.
- The file ends with `MSCFILE_DIRS           =\n` — no trailing blank line at EOF.

### 1.3 Short template (`-s -g`, 421 lines)

Reference bytes: `/workspace/refdata/Doxyfile.short.txt`.

- Line 1: `# Doxyfile 1.17.0`, line 2 blank, then the 18 section banners (same 75-dash rules, same titles, same order).
- **No** per-option comment blocks, **no** explanatory header text.
- All 306 options present, same order, same values, same 23-width alignment, same multi-line continuation format as the full template.
- Layout quirk: no blank line between a section banner and its first option, and no blank line between the last option of a section and the next banner. The only blank lines are line 2 (after the `# Doxyfile 1.17.0` header).
- Tag order in both templates is identical (verified by diff of extracted tag names).

---

## 2. `-u` — update an existing config file

### 2.1 Invocation, message, streams

- `doxygen [-s] -u [name]`: reads `<name>` (default `Doxyfile`), rewrites it in place.
  - stdout: `\n\nConfiguration file '<name>' updated.\n\n` (blank line, blank line, message, blank line). stderr carries only warnings (see 2.4). Exit 0.
- `doxygen [-s] -u -`: reads the config from **stdin**, writes the updated template to **stdout**, with **no** "updated" message and no extra blank lines. Exit 0.
- Missing file: stderr `error: configuration file <name> not found!\n`, the full usage/help text is printed to **stdout**, exit code **1**.
- `-u` output is the full canonical template (or short with `-s`) with user values/comments merged. Verified: `-u` on an empty config produces output **byte-identical** to `-g` (and `-s -u` byte-identical to `-s -g`). `-u` is idempotent: running it on its own output yields byte-identical file.
- Order is always the **canonical template order**; the user's tag order/section order in the input is irrelevant.

### 2.2 How user values are re-emitted

- User values override defaults at the tag's canonical position, emitted with the same 23-width alignment (`TAG<pad>= value`) and continuation format as `-g`.
- Values are re-emitted **verbatim as parsed** — no normalization of case or numbers: `WARNINGS = yes` → `WARNINGS               = yes`; `QUIET = 1` → `QUIET                  = 1`; `CREATE_SUBDIRS_LEVEL = 007` → `007` (not `7`); `EXTRACT_ALL = Yes` keeps capital Y.
- Re-quoting rule: after parsing (one layer of surrounding double quotes removed, inline `\` line-continuations joined, list split on unquoted whitespace), each emitted item that contains a space is wrapped in double quotes; items without spaces are unquoted:
  - `PROJECT_NAME = My Custom Project` → `PROJECT_NAME           = "My Custom Project"`
  - `PROJECT_NAME = "Already Quoted"` → unchanged `"Already Quoted"`
  - `OUTPUT_DIRECTORY = /tmp/some dir` → `"/tmp/some dir"`; trailing whitespace in the input value is trimmed first.
  - Single quotes are ordinary characters: `PROJECT_BRIEF = 'single quotes'` → `"'single quotes'"`.
  - Backslashes are preserved literally: a parsed item `item\ with\ backslash` (backslash-escaped spaces in input) → `"item\ with\ backslash"`.
  - Escaped quotes inside a quoted value survive: `"say \"hi\" there"` → re-emitted unchanged as `"say \"hi\" there"`.
  - Unescaped/unbalanced quote characters are **stripped** and a warning is issued (see 2.4): `1.0 "quoted part"` → `"1.0 quoted part"`; `a"b` → `ab`; `"unbalanced` → `unbalanced`.
  - `TAG = ""` → emitted empty (`TAG =`). Edge cases (verified, obscure): `" "` (one space) → `""`; `"  "` (two spaces) → `" "`.
- Lists: all items (from `=` and any `+=` lines, in order) are re-emitted one item per line with ` \` continuations. `INPUT = src include` + `INPUT += extra dir` → items `src`, `include`, `extra`, `dir`. A later plain `=` assignment **resets** the list (`INPUT = a` / `INPUT += b` / `INPUT = z` → `z` only). Repeated assignment to a scalar: last wins.
- `@INCLUDE = <file>` directives are resolved while reading; the included values are merged and the `@INCLUDE` line itself is **not** preserved — output is flattened.
- Environment variables (`$(VAR)`), `$VAR`, and `%(VAR)s` forms in values are **not** expanded by `-u`; they are re-emitted literally.
- A value identical to the default is still emitted (the user's setting is always written; `-u` never drops a tag).

### 2.3 Comment handling

- `##` (double-hash) comments are preserved and attached to the **next tag** in the input:
  - Full template: emitted after the option's template comment block and a blank line, followed by a blank line, then the tag:
    ```
    # <template comment...>

    ## A user comment about brief

    PROJECT_BRIEF          = ...
    ```
  - Short template (`-s -u`): emitted on the line directly before the tag, no surrounding blank lines.
  - Multiple stacked `##` lines are all preserved, in order.
- Single `#` comments (including any user header at the top of the file and inline `TAG = value # comment` trailers) are **discarded silently**.
- Orphaned `##` comments — those preceding an unknown/obsolete tag that gets dropped, or trailing at EOF with no following tag — are appended at the **end of the output file**, after the last option, preceded by one blank line, in encounter order.

### 2.4 Warnings (stderr) and dropped tags

- Unknown tag: `warning: ignoring unsupported tag '<TAG>' at line <N>, file <name>` — tag and its value dropped. Tag names are **case-sensitive** (`quiet` is unknown). Note `TAB_WIDTH` is unknown (fully removed; not even in the obsolete table), while `TAB_SIZE` is valid.
- Obsolete tag (in `-u` mode), two lines, second line indented with 9 spaces:
  ```
  warning: Tag '<TAG>' at line <N> of file '<name>' has become obsolete.
           This tag has been removed.
  ```
  Observed obsolete tags: `CLASS_DIAGRAMS`, `SHOW_DIRECTORIES`, `SYMBOL_CACHE_SIZE`, `XML_SCHEMA`, `XML_DTD`, `PERL_PATH`, `MSCGEN_PATH`, `HTML_ALIGN_MEMBERS`, `USE_INLINE_TREES`, `DETAILS_AT_TOP`, `MAX_DOT_GRAPH_WIDTH`, `DOT_FONTNAME`, `COLS_IN_ALPHA_INDEX`, `LATEX_SOURCE_CODE`, `RTF_SOURCE_CODE`, `DOCBOOK_PROGRAMLISTING`, `HTML_TIMESTAMP`, `LATEX_TIMESTAMP`, `FORMULA_TRANSPARENT`, `TCL_SUBST`.
- Special migration: `CLASS_DIAGRAMS = NO` additionally changes `CLASS_GRAPH` to `TEXT` and prints `warning: Changing CLASS_GRAPH option to TEXT because obsolete option CLASS_DIAGRAM was found and set to NO.` (note `CLASS_DIAGRAM` without the S in this message). `CLASS_DIAGRAMS = YES` maps to `CLASS_GRAPH = YES` (the default, no extra warning observed).
- Improperly quoted value: `warning: Invalid value for '<TAG>' tag at line <N>, file <name>: Value '<raw value>' is not properly quoted` — value is still used, with the offending quote characters stripped (see 2.2).
- All warnings go to stderr; `-u` still exits 0.

---

## 3. `-x` / `-x_noenv` — diff against defaults

### 3.1 Output form

- `doxygen -x [name]`: prints to **stdout**, exit 0 (even with zero differences), stderr only warnings.
- Exact output: a header line, then one block per differing option. No blank line after the header, no blank lines between options, no trailing blank line (file ends with `\n` after the last option line):
  ```
  # Difference with default Doxyfile 1.17.0 (9135bd68ddc9ea65023d967c75048a7a86a5d495)
  PROJECT_NAME           = "Diff Test"
  QUIET                  = YES
  INPUT                  = src \
                           include
  ```
- Header is exactly `# Difference with default Doxyfile 1.17.0 (9135bd68ddc9ea65023d967c75048a7a86a5d495)`.
- If nothing differs (e.g. empty config, or only default-valued settings), output is just the header line.
- Option lines use the same serialization as the template: tag padded to width 23, `= `, values quoted iff they contain spaces, multi-item lists with 25-space-indented ` \` continuations.
- **Order of printed options is always the canonical template order**, regardless of their order in the input file.
- `-x -` reads the config from stdin; output identical in form. `-s -x` behaves identically to `-x` (there are no comments in the diff anyway).
- Missing file: stderr `error: configuration file <name> not found!\n`, full usage text to stdout, exit **1**.

### 3.2 What counts as "different from default"

Comparison is on the **parsed** value, not the raw text:

- Quoting is normalized: `PROJECT_NAME = My Project` (unquoted) equals the default `"My Project"` → not shown. Whitespace *inside* the value matters: `"My  Project"` (two spaces) → shown.
- Bools compare case-insensitively over the accepted set: `yes`, `Yes`, `YES`, `true`, `1` are equal; `no`, `NO`, `false`, `0` equal. `WARNINGS = yes` (default `YES`) → not shown. Display is verbatim: `EXTRACT_ALL = Yes` (differs from default `NO`) → shown as `EXTRACT_ALL            = Yes`; `QUIET = 1` shown as `1`.
- Ints compare numerically: `CREATE_SUBDIRS_LEVEL = 08` equals default `8` → not shown; but when different, the user's string is shown verbatim (`007` vs default `8` → shown as `007`).
- Enums compare case-insensitively: `OUTPUT_LANGUAGE = english` / `ENGLISH` equal default `English` → not shown.
- Strings compare exactly (after quote-stripping/trimming): `PROJECT_BRIEF = " "` parses to empty, equal to the empty default → not shown.
- Empty vs non-empty: `FILE_PATTERNS =` (empty list, default is the long built-in list) → shown as `FILE_PATTERNS          =`.

# Spec: config_serialize — Doxygen 1.17.0 config template generation, `-u` update, `-x`/`-x_noenv` diff

Binary probed: `/workspace/refdata/original.bin` (Doxygen 1.17.0, commit `9135bd68ddc9ea65023d967c75048a7a86a5d495`).
All outputs verified byte-stable across runs (two `-g -` runs byte-identical; identical to `/workspace/refdata/Doxyfile.full.txt` / `Doxyfile.short.txt`).

Conventions: `<name>` = config file name as given on the command line (default `Doxyfile`). All streams/exit codes verified by redirection.

---

## 1. `-g` template generation

### 1.1 Messages and streams

- `doxygen [-s] -g <name>` (writes a file):
  - File `<name>` is written (existing file **overwritten silently**, no prompt, no backup).
  - stdout, exact bytes (note leading and trailing blank lines):
    ```
    \n\nConfiguration file '<name>' created.\n\nNow edit the configuration file and enter\n\n  doxygen\n\nto generate the documentation for your project\n\n
    ```
    i.e. lines: ``, ``, `Configuration file '<name>' created.`, ``, `Now edit the configuration file and enter`, ``, `  doxygen` (two leading spaces), ``, `to generate the documentation for your project`, ``.
  - stderr empty. Exit code 0.
- `doxygen [-s] -g -` (stdout): writes **only the template** to stdout — no "created" message, no extra blank lines. stderr empty, exit 0.
- The file written by `-g <name>` is byte-identical to the `-g -` stdout output.
- `-s` selects the short template; `-s -g <name>` prints the same "created" message form.

### 1.2 Full template structure (`-g`, 2997 lines)

Reference bytes: `/workspace/refdata/Doxyfile.full.txt`.

Header (lines 1–25), verbatim:

```
# Doxyfile 1.17.0
<blank>
# This file describes the settings to be used by the documentation system
# Doxygen (www.doxygen.org) for a project.
#
# All text after a double hash (##) is considered a comment and is placed in
# front of the TAG it is preceding.
#
# All text after a single hash (#) is considered a comment and will be ignored.
# The format is:
# TAG = value [value, ...]
# For lists, items can also be appended using:
# TAG += value [value, ...]
# Values that contain spaces should be placed between quotes (\" \").
#
# Note:
#
# Use Doxygen to compare the used configuration file with the template
# configuration file:
# doxygen -x [configFile]
# Use Doxygen to compare the used configuration file with the template
# configuration file without replacing the environment variables or CMake type
# replacement variables:
# doxygen -x_noenv [configFile]
<blank>
```

Then 18 sections. Each section is a 3-line banner; in the **full** template the banner is preceded and followed by one blank line:

```
#---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# <Section title>
#---------------------------------------------------------------------------
```

The banner rule line is exactly `#` + 75 dashes. Section titles, in order:

1. `Project related configuration options`
2. `Build related configuration options`
3. `Configuration options related to warning and progress messages`
4. `Configuration options related to the input files`
5. `Configuration options related to source browsing`
6. `Configuration options related to the alphabetical class index`
7. `Configuration options related to the HTML output`
8. `Configuration options related to the LaTeX output`
9. `Configuration options related to the RTF output`
10. `Configuration options related to the man page output`
11. `Configuration options related to the XML output`
12. `Configuration options related to the DOCBOOK output`
13. `Configuration options for the AutoGen Definitions output`
14. `Configuration options related to Sqlite3 output`
15. `Configuration options related to the Perl module output`
16. `Configuration options related to the preprocessor`
17. `Configuration options related to external references`
18. `Configuration options related to diagram generator tools`

Per-option block in the full template:

```
# <comment line 1>
# <comment line ...>
<blank>
TAG<padding>= <value>
<blank>
```

- 306 options total, all emitted **active** (there are NO commented-out `# TAG = default` template options in 1.17.0; the only `# TAG = ...` lines are examples inside comment prose, e.g. `# MATHJAX_EXTENSIONS = ams`).
- **Alignment**: the tag name is left-justified padded with spaces to width 23, then `=`. So `=` is always at byte column 24 (1-based). The two 23-char tags (`HIDE_COMPOUND_REFERENCE`, `GENERATE_DEPRECATEDLIST`) get zero padding: `HIDE_COMPOUND_REFERENCE= NO`. Format equivalent to `printf("%-23s= ...")` — no extra space if tag length ≥ 23 (none exist longer in 1.17.0).
- Empty values: line ends right after `=`, **no trailing space** (`PROJECT_NUMBER         =\n`). Verified: zero lines with trailing whitespace in the whole template.
- Value starts at column 26 (after `= `).
- Multi-line (list) values: first item on the tag line; each subsequent item on its own line, indented with 25 spaces (item starts at column 26, aligned under the first item); every line except the last ends with ` \` (space + backslash); last item has no backslash. Exactly 59 continuation lines in the full template. Example:

```
ABBREVIATE_BRIEF       = "The $name class" \
                         "The $name widget" \
                         ...
                         the
```

- Quoting of defaults: a value/item containing a space is wrapped in double quotes (`PROJECT_NAME           = "My Project"`, `"The $name class"`); items without spaces are unquoted (`English`, `*.c`).
- Comment block conventions (generated from option metadata):
  - `The default value is: <value>.` — 193 options, final line of the comment for string/int/bool options with a non-empty scalar default. The `<value>` here is shown **unquoted** even when the emitted default is quoted (e.g. comment says `The default value is: My Project.` while the tag line is `PROJECT_NAME           = "My Project"`).
  - `Minimum value: <n>, maximum value: <n>, default value: <n>.` — 21 int options with ranges.
  - `Possible values are: ...` — 15 enum-ish options (list may wrap over several comment lines).
  - `This tag requires that the tag <TAG> is set to <VAL>.` — 147 occurrences (dependency notes; `<VAL>` observed: `YES`).
  - One special: `# Note: This tag requires that UML_LOOK isn't set, i.e. the Doxygen internal` (wraps to next line; for `UML_LOOK`-adjacent option).
  - `See also: <TAG>` lines appear for some options.
- The file ends with `MSCFILE_DIRS           =\n` — no trailing blank line at EOF.

### 1.3 Short template (`-s -g`, 421 lines)

Reference bytes: `/workspace/refdata/Doxyfile.short.txt`.

- Line 1: `# Doxyfile 1.17.0`, line 2 blank, then the 18 section banners (same 75-dash rules, same titles, same order).
- **No** per-option comment blocks, **no** explanatory header text.
- All 306 options present, same order, same values, same 23-width alignment, same multi-line continuation format as the full template.
- Layout quirk: no blank line between a section banner and its first option, and no blank line between the last option of a section and the next banner. The only blank lines are line 2 (after the `# Doxyfile 1.17.0` header).
- Tag order in both templates is identical (verified by diff of extracted tag names).

---

## 2. `-u` — update an existing config file

### 2.1 Invocation, message, streams

- `doxygen [-s] -u [name]`: reads `<name>` (default `Doxyfile`), rewrites it in place.
  - stdout: `\n\nConfiguration file '<name>' updated.\n\n` (blank line, blank line, message, blank line). stderr carries only warnings (see 2.4). Exit 0.
- `doxygen [-s] -u -`: reads the config from **stdin**, writes the updated template to **stdout**, with **no** "updated" message and no extra blank lines. Exit 0.
- Missing file: stderr `error: configuration file <name> not found!\n`, the full usage/help text is printed to **stdout**, exit code **1**.
- `-u` output is the full canonical template (or short with `-s`) with user values/comments merged. Verified: `-u` on an empty config produces output **byte-identical** to `-g` (and `-s -u` byte-identical to `-s -g`). `-u` is idempotent: running it on its own output yields byte-identical file.
- Order is always the **canonical template order**; the user's tag order/section order in the input is irrelevant.

### 2.2 How user values are re-emitted

- User values override defaults at the tag's canonical position, emitted with the same 23-width alignment (`TAG<pad>= value`) and continuation format as `-g`.
- Values are re-emitted **verbatim as parsed** — no normalization of case or numbers: `WARNINGS = yes` → `WARNINGS               = yes`; `QUIET = 1` → `QUIET                  = 1`; `CREATE_SUBDIRS_LEVEL = 007` → `007` (not `7`); `EXTRACT_ALL = Yes` keeps capital Y.
- Re-quoting rule: after parsing (one layer of surrounding double quotes removed, inline `\` line-continuations joined, list split on unquoted whitespace), each emitted item that contains a space is wrapped in double quotes; items without spaces are unquoted:
  - `PROJECT_NAME = My Custom Project` → `PROJECT_NAME           = "My Custom Project"`
  - `PROJECT_NAME = "Already Quoted"` → unchanged `"Already Quoted"`
  - `OUTPUT_DIRECTORY = /tmp/some dir` → `"/tmp/some dir"`; trailing whitespace in the input value is trimmed first.
  - Single quotes are ordinary characters: `PROJECT_BRIEF = 'single quotes'` → `"'single quotes'"`.
  - Backslashes are preserved literally: a parsed item `item\ with\ backslash` (backslash-escaped spaces in input) → `"item\ with\ backslash"`.
  - Escaped quotes inside a quoted value survive: `"say \"hi\" there"` → re-emitted unchanged as `"say \"hi\" there"`.
  - Unescaped/unbalanced quote characters are **stripped** and a warning is issued (see 2.4): `1.0 "quoted part"` → `"1.0 quoted part"`; `a"b` → `ab`; `"unbalanced` → `unbalanced`.
  - `TAG = ""` → emitted empty (`TAG =`). Edge cases (verified, obscure): `" "` (one space) → `""`; `"  "` (two spaces) → `" "`.
- Lists: all items (from `=` and any `+=` lines, in order) are re-emitted one item per line with ` \` continuations. `INPUT = src include` + `INPUT += extra dir` → items `src`, `include`, `extra`, `dir`. A later plain `=` assignment **resets** the list (`INPUT = a` / `INPUT += b` / `INPUT = z` → `z` only). Repeated assignment to a scalar: last wins.
- `@INCLUDE = <file>` directives are resolved while reading; the included values are merged and the `@INCLUDE` line itself is **not** preserved — output is flattened.
- Environment variables (`$(VAR)`), `$VAR`, and `%(VAR)s` forms in values are **not** expanded by `-u`; they are re-emitted literally.
- A value identical to the default is still emitted (the user's setting is always written; `-u` never drops a tag).

### 2.3 Comment handling

- `##` (double-hash) comments are preserved and attached to the **next tag** in the input:
  - Full template: emitted after the option's template comment block and a blank line, followed by a blank line, then the tag:
    ```
    # <template comment...>

    ## A user comment about brief

    PROJECT_BRIEF          = ...
    ```
  - Short template (`-s -u`): emitted on the line directly before the tag, no surrounding blank lines.
  - Multiple stacked `##` lines are all preserved, in order.
- Single `#` comments (including any user header at the top of the file and inline `TAG = value # comment` trailers) are **discarded silently**.
- Orphaned `##` comments — those preceding an unknown/obsolete tag that gets dropped, or trailing at EOF with no following tag — are appended at the **end of the output file**, after the last option, preceded by one blank line, in encounter order.

### 2.4 Warnings (stderr) and dropped tags

- Unknown tag: `warning: ignoring unsupported tag '<TAG>' at line <N>, file <name>` — tag and its value dropped. Tag names are **case-sensitive** (`quiet` is unknown). Note `TAB_WIDTH` is unknown (fully removed; not even in the obsolete table), while `TAB_SIZE` is valid.
- Obsolete tag (in `-u` mode), two lines, second line indented with 9 spaces:
  ```
  warning: Tag '<TAG>' at line <N> of file '<name>' has become obsolete.
           This tag has been removed.
  ```
  Observed obsolete tags: `CLASS_DIAGRAMS`, `SHOW_DIRECTORIES`, `SYMBOL_CACHE_SIZE`, `XML_SCHEMA`, `XML_DTD`, `PERL_PATH`, `MSCGEN_PATH`, `HTML_ALIGN_MEMBERS`, `USE_INLINE_TREES`, `DETAILS_AT_TOP`, `MAX_DOT_GRAPH_WIDTH`, `DOT_FONTNAME`, `COLS_IN_ALPHA_INDEX`, `LATEX_SOURCE_CODE`, `RTF_SOURCE_CODE`, `DOCBOOK_PROGRAMLISTING`, `HTML_TIMESTAMP`, `LATEX_TIMESTAMP`, `FORMULA_TRANSPARENT`, `TCL_SUBST`.
- Special migration: `CLASS_DIAGRAMS = NO` additionally changes `CLASS_GRAPH` to `TEXT` and prints `warning: Changing CLASS_GRAPH option to TEXT because obsolete option CLASS_DIAGRAM was found and set to NO.` (note `CLASS_DIAGRAM` without the S in this message). `CLASS_DIAGRAMS = YES` maps to `CLASS_GRAPH = YES` (the default, no extra warning observed).
- Improperly quoted value: `warning: Invalid value for '<TAG>' tag at line <N>, file <name>: Value '<raw value>' is not properly quoted` — value is still used, with the offending quote characters stripped (see 2.2).
- All warnings go to stderr; `-u` still exits 0.

---

## 3. `-x` / `-x_noenv` — diff against defaults

### 3.1 Output form

- `doxygen -x [name]`: prints to **stdout**, exit 0 (even with zero differences), stderr only warnings.
- Exact output: a header line, then one block per differing option. No blank line after the header, no blank lines between options, no trailing blank line (file ends with `\n` after the last option line):
  ```
  # Difference with default Doxyfile 1.17.0 (9135bd68ddc9ea65023d967c75048a7a86a5d495)
  PROJECT_NAME           = "Diff Test"
  QUIET                  = YES
  INPUT                  = src \
                           include
  ```
- Header is exactly `# Difference with default Doxyfile 1.17.0 (9135bd68ddc9ea65023d967c75048a7a86a5d495)`.
- If nothing differs (e.g. empty config, or only default-valued settings), output is just the header line.
- Option lines use the same serialization as the template: tag padded to width 23, `= `, values quoted iff they contain spaces, multi-item lists with 25-space-indented ` \` continuations.
- **Order of printed options is always the canonical template order**, regardless of their order in the input file.
- `-x -` reads the config from stdin; output identical in form. `-s -x` behaves identically to `-x` (there are no comments in the diff anyway).
- Missing file: stderr `error: configuration file <name> not found!\n`, full usage text to stdout, exit **1**.

### 3.2 What counts as "different from default"

Comparison is on the **parsed** value, not the raw text:

- Quoting is normalized: `PROJECT_NAME = My Project` (unquoted) equals the default `"My Project"` → not shown. Whitespace *inside* the value matters: `"My  Project"` (two spaces) → shown.
- Bools compare case-insensitively over the accepted set: `yes`, `Yes`, `YES`, `true`, `1` are equal; `no`, `NO`, `false`, `0` equal. `WARNINGS = yes` (default `YES`) → not shown. Display is verbatim: `EXTRACT_ALL = Yes` (differs from default `NO`) → shown as `EXTRACT_ALL            = Yes`; `QUIET = 1` shown as `1`.
- Ints compare numerically: `CREATE_SUBDIRS_LEVEL = 08` equals default `8` → not shown; but when different, the user's string is shown verbatim (`007` vs default `8` → shown as `007`).
- Enums compare case-insensitively: `OUTPUT_LANGUAGE = english` / `ENGLISH` equal default `English` → not shown.
- Strings compare exactly (after quote-stripping/trimming): `PROJECT_BRIEF = " "` parses to empty, equal to the empty default → not shown.
- Empty vs non-empty: `FILE_PATTERNS =` (empty list, default is the long built-in list) → shown as `FILE_PATTERNS          =`.
- `TAG += ...` appends to the **default** list; `-x` then shows the full effective list (defaults + appended items), e.g. `FILE_PATTERNS += *.foo *.bar` prints all default patterns followed by `*.foo \` / `*.bar`.
- Repeated assignment: last `=` wins; the tag appears at most once, at its template position.
- Unknown tags: warning on stderr, not in the diff. Obsolete tags: warning on stderr (different second line than `-u`, see below); migrations still apply (`CLASS_DIAGRAMS = NO` → diff shows `CLASS_GRAPH            = TEXT`).
- Obsolete-tag warning outside `-u` mode:
  ```
  warning: Tag '<TAG>' at line <N> of file '<name>' has become obsolete.
           To avoid this warning please remove this line from your configuration file or upgrade it using "doxygen -u"
  ```
  (second line indented 9 spaces).

### 3.3 Environment variable expansion (`-x` vs `-x_noenv`)

- `-x` expands `$(VAR)` in values using the process environment **before** comparing/printing; `-x_noenv` leaves values unexpanded. Example with `MYDIR=/tmp/envdir`:
  - input `OUTPUT_DIRECTORY = $(MYDIR)/docs`
  - `-x` → `OUTPUT_DIRECTORY       = /tmp/envdir/docs`
  - `-x_noenv` → `OUTPUT_DIRECTORY       = $(MYDIR)/docs`
- Only the `$(VAR)` form is expanded. Bare `$VAR` is **not** expanded (`$HOME/plain` stays literal under `-x`).
- `%(VAR)s` (CMake-style) is **not** expanded in tag values under either `-x` or `-x_noenv` (observed literal `%(HOME)s` / `%(MYNAME)s` in output even with the variable set), despite the usage text mentioning CMake-type replacement variables.
- Undefined `$(VAR)` expands to the empty string silently (no warning): `$(UNDEF)/d` → `/d`; in a list, `$(UNDEF_A) x $(UNDEF_B)` → single item `x`.
- Expansion happens per-item before list splitting/quoting.

---

## 4. Quick message template reference

| Context | Stream | Exact text (placeholders in `<>`), trailing `\n` on every line |
|---|---|---|
| `-g <name>` | stdout | `\n\nConfiguration file '<name>' created.\n\nNow edit the configuration file and enter\n\n  doxygen\n\nto generate the documentation for your project\n\n` |
| `-u <name>` | stdout | `\n\nConfiguration file '<name>' updated.\n\n` |
| `-g -` / `-u -` | stdout | template only, no message |
| missing config (any mode) | stderr | `error: configuration file <name> not found!` (+ usage text on stdout, exit 1) |
| unknown tag | stderr | `warning: ignoring unsupported tag '<TAG>' at line <N>, file <name>` |
| obsolete tag, `-u` | stderr | `warning: Tag '<TAG>' at line <N> of file '<name>' has become obsolete.\n         This tag has been removed.` |
| obsolete tag, `-x`/run | stderr | `warning: Tag '<TAG>' at line <N> of file '<name>' has become obsolete.\n         To avoid this warning please remove this line from your configuration file or upgrade it using "doxygen -u"` |
| bad quoting | stderr | `warning: Invalid value for '<TAG>' tag at line <N>, file <name>: Value '<raw>' is not properly quoted` |
| CLASS_DIAGRAMS=NO | stderr | `warning: Changing CLASS_GRAPH option to TEXT because obsolete option CLASS_DIAGRAM was found and set to NO.` |
| `-x` header | stdout | `# Difference with default Doxyfile 1.17.0 (9135bd68ddc9ea65023d967c75048a7a86a5d495)` |
